question.prompt: Suppose that \[\dfrac{2x}{3} - \dfrac{x}{6}\] is an integer. Which of the following statements must be true about \(x?\)

solutions.explanation:
Combining the two terms reveals what the integer condition means:
\[
\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{x}{6}
=\frac{4x-x}{6}
=\frac{x}{2}.
\]
If this value is an integer \(k\), then \(x=2k\), so \(x\) must be an even integer. Conversely, every \(x=2k\) with integer \(k\) makes the expression an integer.

The allowed value \(x=2\) is positive and is not a multiple of \(3\), \(6\), or \(12\). Thus none of the stronger restrictions in the other choices is forced. The answer is B.
solutions.title: Simplify the integer condition
